thread:
elaine: Quick idea 1000 1000 Trying a right-side 'sidecar' walkthrough instead of a full-width banner for first-run. It would step users through: 1) checklist, 2) sample apps, 3) API keys. Keeps the main canvas visible. Thoughts? :sparkles:

diego: I like non-blocking stuff. As long as it doesn't steal focus when it appears. Modals are easier for forcing completion but kill context. Sidecar seems lighter.

rachel: Agree with diego. Two UX notes: a) show micro-previews of sample apps (tiny thumbnail + 1-line summary) so people know what they'll get, b) lazy-load assets so the sidecar opens instantly.

elaine: For the micro-previews I was thinking a collapsed card that expands inline when hovered/focused. Also add a small "try preview" button that launches a read-only preview workspace.

sam: Metric-wise we should measure time-to-first-api-call, sample-preview-clicks, and onboarding-completion. Can we gate the preview behind a feature flag so we can A/B test with/without the preview button?

a11y-bot: Accessibility reminders: ensure sidecar is reachable by keyboard, focus trap only when user explicitly chooses "Guide me" (not on appear), announce step changes with aria-live, and provide skip links. Also color contrast check for thumbnail captions.

diego: UX copy for the CTA: instead of "Get started" try context-specific CTAs like "Try FinOps sample" or "Create demo workspace". More specific CTAs = better conversion.

rachel: Copy tweak: the first-run checklist header should say "Quick setup (5 mins)" 1000 adds perceived low time commitment.

elaine: Implementation thought: collapsed sidecar shows a pill like "Welcome 1000 3 steps" with a subtle pulse on first visit for 6s. Clicking expands to the stepper. Pulse should be motion-reduced if user prefers reduced motion.

sam: For telemetry consent: only fire the "sidecar_pulse_shown" event after the consent modal is accepted. We can still show it but don't record the event until allowed. Add a fallback count in localStorage for unauthenticated visitors.

a11y-bot: For screen readers: provide an aria-label on the sidecar toggle and ensure the "preview workspace" button has aria-describedby that explains it won't create persistent billing resources.

diego: Performance asks: prefetch only metadata for samples (titles, thumbnails). Defer large asset downloads until user chooses import. Use progressive placeholders.

rachel: Small accessibility copy change: change "Import project" to "Create demo workspace" and add subtext "Sandboxed, free to delete". That reduces fear.

elaine: I'll mock up two variants: Variant A = sidecar with preview button; Variant B = sidecar without preview but bigger thumbnails. We'll ship behind flags and test CTAs. @sam can you own the flag and metrics? @diego will coordinate lazy-loading. @rachel I'll need those microcopy strings.

sam: Yep I'll add flags and track the funnel. Suggested metrics: preview->import conversion, import failure rate, time to interactive after import.

a11y-bot: Suggested QA checklist to add in PR template: 1) keyboard nav verification, 2) screen reader walkthrough, 3) high-contrast mode check, 4) reduced-motion check, 5) aria-live announcements for step changes.

elaine: Perfect. I'll post mocks in the design folder and a short prototype link. Will also include the microcopy and a11y checklist in the PR desc. Thanks :raised_hands:
